findings.text: non-blocking: the replacement's lease on the published image is released by _stop_locked (:1761, _release_image_pin) and only re-taken at :1633, so the image is unleased for the whole stop (one SERVICE_STOP_GRACE_SECONDS=10 s wait, plus a second after SIGKILL); a concurrent materialize_committed_tree prune that finds it unheld can remove it, which is the failure the new lease exists to prevent. The window is narrow because retention is COMMITTED_TREE_RETENTION=3 (checkout_trust.py:52) and the image has just been stamped newest, so three further identities must be published inside the stop for it to rank into the prune slice; but when it does happen _pin_image catches the OSError, logs, and starts the copy anyway with PYTHONPATH naming the removed tree, so the copy resolves the next entry on the path rather than refusing. Carrying the existing descriptor across the stop (capture state.image_pin and clear it before _stop_locked, assign it to the replacement) would leave no gap in the lease.
